species.name: Barnaclet

dex.text: A goose-neck barnacle on a plank of driftwood, with a long neck and a hopeful expression. If you wait, it might hatch into something with feathers.
dex.fact: Medieval people believed barnacle geese grew from goose barnacles on driftwood, and so the church treated the geese as fish for fast days.

species.real: Goose barnacles are crustaceans, relatives of crabs, and as adults spend their lives glued by their heads to one spot.

species.name: Barnagoose

dex.text: Hatched out of its plank at last, all black neck and white face, and very sure that this is the right way round. Gerald of Wales would be thrilled.
dex.fact: Gerald of Wales wrote about barnacle geese in the twelfth century, and the real birds breed in the Arctic and winter in places such as the Solway Firth and Islay.

species.real: The real barnacle goose nests on cliff ledges in the Arctic, and its goslings jump from the cliff a few days after hatching.
